identity_boundary: GlyNAC is a distinct glycine-plus-NAC combination; no efficacy inheritance by glycine or NAC alone.

sources.title: Glycine increases fat-free mass in malnourished haemodialysis patients: a randomized double-blind crossover trial
sources.reading_depth: Complete scientific main and declarations; all main table text; native Figure 1 and Tables 1 and 4. Current registry scientific fields. Supplement captions only; no actual supplement read.

design.type: Randomized, double-blind, active-comparator crossover; reported post hoc secondary analysis
design.missingness: One withdrew before baseline and allocation was reassigned; nine of 36 starters were not in the 27-person complete-crossover analysis. Full loss reasons were not enumerated in the main read. No ITT estimate qualified.

population.description: Maintenance haemodialysis adults with features of protein-energy wasting

preparations.glycine: 7 g granule packs twice daily, 30 minutes before breakfast and dinner, 14 g/day orally
preparations.comparator: BCAA per pack leucine 3.62 g, valine 1.94 g, isoleucine 1.45 g; twice daily
preparations.manufacturer_packaging: Bichsel pharmacy, Interlaken; Ivers-Lee, Burgdorf; matched appearance/taste and cGMP packaging
preparations.identity_boundary: Biologically active BCAA comparison, no inert or unsupplemented period; no retail-product equivalence
preparations.compliance: More than 80% of packs in each period, assessed by returned empty/full packs

analyses.model: Supplement, month, period, age and sex fixed effects; participant random intercept; some outcomes transformed for normality
analyses.multiplicity: Benjamini–Hochberg; Table 4 supplement significance threshold below .005
analyses.carryover: Not tested; nonsignificant period×month interaction and washout do not prove absence of carryover
analyses.hierarchy: Post hoc secondary analysis. Current registry has microbiota primary, with body composition and physical outcomes among many secondary measures. Original registry history/SAP not read.
analyses.registration_timing: First submitted 2016-08-23, first posted 2016-11-11, study start 2016-08 (main 2016-08-01); current record does not establish prospective public posting.
analyses.power_limit: Secondary lean-mass sample-size assumption derived from a different large comparison; adequate power for each functional outcome not established.

controlled_results.interpretation: Positive comparative BIA signal favouring glycine; survives reported supplement multiplicity correction; not a direct muscle-protein or force measure

controlled_results.endpoint: BIA fat-free mass index, baseline-adjusted model

controlled_results.interpretation: Nonpositive; DXA definition includes lean soft tissue and bone mineral
Table coefficient and footnote are positive for glycine, while abstract/Results prose says weight did not differ. Preserve discrepancy, not an unqualified weight null or benefit.

controlled_results.endpoint: Handgrip, pedometry and quality of life
controlled_results.source: Complete main Results; detailed supplement not accessed
controlled_results.interpretation: Main reports no between-supplement differences. Detailed numeric estimates/CIs not independently qualified.

within_period_results.unit: Square-root transformed grip scale; not kg
within_period_results.limit: Selected within-period result; not randomized treatment contrast; transform identified in Figure S2 caption, actual supplement not read

within_period_results.endpoint: BIA fat-free mass index, glycine month 4 versus baseline
within_period_results.limit: Within-period result, separate from controlled coefficient

sources.assays_and_transfer: No muscle biopsy, BUBR1, chromosome-fidelity or variant-rescue assay reported in main. Plasma glycine did not rise at sampled visits; timing explanation is speculative. BIA fluid/protein composition remains unresolved despite post-dialysis measurement and fluid-status observations.

harms.nuance: Discussion describes six glycine patients, three also symptomatic during washout; causal attribution uncertain. Fluid-overload supplemental dialysis clustered in four patients. No significant reported AE difference is not proof of safety equivalence.

sources.funding_conflicts: Swiss National Science Foundation, Alfred and Alice Lachmann Foundation, Fresenius Kabi; stated no funder role. Genton/Teta industry relationships; Cani biotech cofounder and patent interests.

sources.title: The effect of enteral glycine on plasma glycine and muscle structure, size, and function in the critically ill: A randomized controlled trial
sources.reading_depth: Complete abstract, public publisher-indexed scientific excerpts and Figure 3 caption, metadata, current registry displayed scientific fields. No complete main, native outcome table/figure, actual supplement or separate SAP.
sources.access_status: Publisher marks OA CC BY4.0. HTML routes403/challenge; PDF open failed; publisher API200 contains metadata only; native-image and possible-supplement URLs403. Technical access limitation, not paywall proof or negative efficacy.

design.type: Blinded randomized parallel three groups in mechanically ventilated adults
design.duration: Until extubation or at most seven days
design.functional_missingness: Only assessable patients described; exact handling of inability to participate, death and missing follow-up unverified

No effect reported; native table/figure unavailable

registry.history_limit: Current displays only, no original archived version. Same-URL renderings differ in last-update display; no endpoint-change inference. No supporting document attached.

notice_check: Exact DOI/title identities verified; same-run Crossref no update-to/relation notices and exact-DOI notice searches did not surface correction/retraction. Bounded, not exhaustive.
